task_and_failure: The two required whole-suite jobs run the whole unittest suite (9,800 tests at base 56473e4b by discovery) in one process. In plan W1's samples (2026-10-02/03, not re-measured here) validate-macos (adoption-bootstrap.yml, macos-15) took a median 1,842 s for its full-suite step and 2,270 s per job over 8 successful pull request runs, and validate (validate.yml, ubuntu-24.04) took 1,727 to 1,828 s per job against its 2,400 s limit. This trial asks whether craigahobbs/unittest-parallel 1.8.6 runs the same tests with the same outcomes in less time on the actual runners. Blocker B1: tests/test_native_maintenance.py loaded six TestCase classes under bare module names inside load_tests, which a spawned worker cannot pickle. The trial head carries the fix, which only prefixes those classes' 29 test ids. Status planned: nothing has run on a GitHub-hosted runner for this record, and nothing is adopted.
discovery_provenance: Plan W1 of 2026-10-03, a coordinator's approved plan kept outside the repository. Its inputs were an Opus design agent at base 56473e4b, an Opus completeness critic and a read-only Codex gpt-6.1-sol cross-family review. Its search-first comparison covered unittest-parallel, pytest-xdist, pytest-split, pytest-testmon, GitHub background steps and matrix sharding, and it decided on compatibility evidence (load_tests, the id set, the log format, lock size), not on popularity.

Three units built the trial in separate worktrees at 56473e4b. U1 is the B1 fix in tests/test_native_maintenance.py. U2 is the oracle in this directory: ids.py, compare.py, the controls and fixtures from real local runs. U3 is .github/workflows/macos-suite-parallel-trial.yml and the two hash-locked lock files. Integration on branch foundation/macos-suite-parallelism-trial-20261003 aligned the workflow with the oracle's run contract in four ways. It passes --expected-sha. It adds a clean-checkout check, because compare.py never reads git-status.txt. It runs the oracle's own tests on the compare job's interpreter. It installs the lock in the inventory job.

The integrator re-verified these facts on 2026-10-03 with read-only GETs. github/docs at the pinned commits: for pull requests, a paths filter compares the three-dot diff between the head and the merge base (triggering-a-workflow-paths5.md). A pull_request run's GITHUB_SHA is the last merge commit (events-that-trigger-workflows.md), so every job checks out and asserts github.event.pull_request.head.sha. The workflow-syntax page documents strategy.max-parallel and step timeout-minutes.
license_and_compatibility: unittest-parallel 1.8.6 is MIT. coverage 7.16.2 is Apache-2.0 and is its only hard dependency. Both are installed from hash-locked official PyPI wheels with --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes (.github/requirements-ci-suite-macos.txt and .github/requirements-ci-suite-linux.txt), and both locks are listed in .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json. Compatibility: unittest-parallel discovers with the stock unittest loader, so the ids are the same, load_tests is honoured and the per-test -v lines and the Ran/status summary are kept. It runs each suite in a spawned process, so every TestCase class must be importable by its module name (B1). Module level keeps module fixtures once per module. Class level runs setUpModule once per class, possibly concurrently (upstream README, 'Parallelism Level'); thirteen test modules define setUpModule. The coverage wheel installs a1_coverage.pth, which stays inert unless COVERAGE_PROCESS_START or COVERAGE_PROCESS_CONFIG is set; the lock is installed in every arm, S included.

baseline_and_candidate.baseline: Arm S on each runner: python3 -m unittest -v --durations 25 from the checkout root, with the trial lock installed. That is the production whole-suite command (validate-macos runs python3 -m unittest -v; validate runs python3 -m unittest) plus -v for per-test lines and --durations 25 as the plan's diagnostic for dominant modules.
baseline_and_candidate.candidate: unittest-parallel 1.8.6 arms, each with -v from the checkout root. On macos-15: P3 (-j 3 --level module), P3F (P3 plus --disable-process-pooling), P3C (-j 3 --level class) and P4 (-j 4 --level module). On ubuntu-24.04: L4 (-j 4 --level module), L4F (L4 plus --disable-process-pooling) and L4C (-j 4 --level class).

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: Fixed before any hosted run. CORPUS: the whole suite at the draft pull request's head SHA on actual GitHub-hosted macos-15 and ubuntu-24.04 runners. Every job asserts that SHA, because a pull_request checkout is otherwise the merge commit. The trial lock is installed in every arm. Each arm runs three times (fail-fast false; max-parallel 2 on macOS and 4 on Linux; repeat-major order, rotated by one arm per repeat). ORACLE PART 1 is compare.py with its README rules, as frozen here, run with --expected-sha set to the head. An arm-run is ineligible on any of these: (a) a missing or invalid log.txt, exit-code.txt or meta.json; (b) meta.json disagreeing with its directory name; (c) a command outside the arm's preregistered flags; (d) a checkout_sha other than the head, or a python_version other than S's on that OS; (e) a truncated log or a failed self-consistency check (started tests equal Ran N, records per outcome equal the status line, the status word agrees with the counts, the error report lists exactly the failing records); (f) an exit status that disagrees with the status line, compared as zero versus non-zero only; (g) a unittest-parallel header that is missing (parallel) or present (serial), or a worker count other than min(suites, jobs); (h) executed ids that are not exactly the trial inventory (ids.py on the head), so every id of the seven gate-step modules must run; (i) any (test id, outcome) record that differs from the first eligible S run of that OS. Ids whose records differ among the eligible S repeats are flaky ids: they are excluded from (i), listed in result.json and named in the observed record. ORACLE PART 2 is the workflow's clean-checkout step (checkout-status.json): every run directory's git-status.txt exists and is empty. A dirty or unrecorded run makes its arm ineligible. ID MAPPING: result.json id_mapping.ok must be true. The base and trial inventories may differ only by the B1 rewrite of six classes, as a bijection; otherwise neither OS gets a verdict. CONTROLS run in separate jobs for every arm, S included. The control file alone in an empty directory must report exactly control_expectations.json's standalone run: Ran 8; FAILED (failures=2, errors=2, skipped=1, expected failures=1, unexpected successes=1); a non-zero exit; the listed pass, skip, failure, error, failing-subtest, expected-failure, unexpected-success, multi-line-docstring and setUpClass-error records; and, in parallel, a header of 1 module suite or 3 class suites over 9 tests. The crash control (os._exit(3)) under a 300 s bound must start, exit non-zero and print no OK summary; a hang ended by the bound is fail-closed and passes. DECISION RULE, per OS. An arm is eligible only when it has at least three runs, every run is eligible under both oracle parts (zero mismatches), and its controls and crash control passed. S must be eligible, or the OS gets no verdict. Take the fastest eligible parallel arm by median step seconds. Adopt it only if its median is at most 0.60 times the S median and its maximum is at most 0.75 times S's fastest run; otherwise reject, with no fall-through to a slower arm. If the adopted arm is P3 (L4 on Linux), take P3F (L4F) instead when it is eligible, meets the rule and its median is at most 1.10 times the pooled median. A reject or a no-verdict outcome is kept as a failed attempt. The macOS verdict decides PR-A and the Linux verdict PR-A2, independently. METRICS: the selection metric is the test step's seconds, meta.json step_seconds (the in-step wall clock around the command) as compare.py reads it. For every run the observed record also keeps the Actions jobs API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs) started_at and completed_at for the test step and for the whole job (job seconds). These are reported beside the rule's input and are not used by the rule.
predeclared_metrics.usage_rule: No usage claim. The hosted runs execute deterministic commands and no model. Observed runs carry no provider usage: their usage fields are observed zeros for deterministic execution, never a savings claim. The model usage of the planning, unit-building and integration sessions is not recorded here and stays unknown; it is neither estimated nor counted as zero. Runner minutes on the public repository's standard runners are not billed (plan W1; not re-measured here).

runtime_and_platform.isolation: A draft pull request that is never merged. The workflow triggers only on pull_request changes to its own file and runs with contents: read, persist-credentials false and no secrets. Each job runs on a fresh hosted VM. The controls run in separate jobs, with each control file copied alone into an empty directory under RUNNER_TEMP and never into tests/. Results stay under RUNNER_TEMP and in artifacts with 30-day retention. No required check, ruleset or production workflow changes.

limitations: Planned only. No GitHub-hosted run exists for this record. The evidence so far is local integration evidence and synthetic fixtures. U1 checked spawned-worker pickling of tests.test_native_maintenance before and after the fix (29 tests). U2 parsed control logs from real local runs on WSL2 with CPython 3.13.16. The integrator ran on 2026-10-03 under CPython 3.13.16 and a uv-managed 3.12.3: test_compare.py (28 tests OK on both), ids.py (9,800 ids at the head, identical on both interpreters, with and without the lock, from tests/ or from the root), and the base-to-trial id mapping (29 ids, 6 classes, ok). The integrator also reproduced the Linux control step locally under CPython 3.12.3 with the Linux lock, with the crash bound shortened to 30 s, and all eight control runs passed compare.py's checks. None of this is upstream acceptance.
The plan's local Linux preflight (python3 -m unittest_parallel -j 3 -v over the whole suite in a worktree) has not run for this record. No whole-suite parallel run has happened anywhere yet.

One trial inventory, generated on ubuntu-24.04 with the lock, serves both runners. That macOS discovery matches is evidenced only at the base (U2's comparison with the Ran 9800 log of run 37073310931). A platform difference would make every macOS run ineligible, S included, which is fail-closed and yields no verdict.

The trial environment is not production's. The macOS arms add the two npm pins (tree-sitter-bash, yaml) that validate.yml installs, because their tripwires fail in any job that is not a recorded gap. validate-macos is a recorded gap (tests/test_shell_parser_ci.py KNOWN_UNPROVISIONED), so those tests skip in production and run in the trial. The macOS arms also skip validate-macos's validators and bootstrap/recording smoke. The Linux arms reproduce only the four suite-environment steps of validate.yml. Every arm adds -v, which Linux production lacks, and S adds --durations 25.

Class-level arms (P3C, L4C) change module-fixture semantics: setUpModule runs once per class. A fixture failure shows up as extra records, but side effects that leave outcomes unchanged are invisible to the oracle.

The crash control's bound is GNU timeout (exit 124) or, where the image lacks it, a perl alarm (exit 142); that macos-15 has timeout is not verified. A pool worker that dies hangs unittest-parallel 1.8.6 until the bound fires, so the controls show that the arm fails closed, not that a crash is reported quickly. The timed arm steps carry their own step timeouts (80 min on macOS, 60 min on Linux).

Ids that flake among the S repeats are excluded from the per-id comparison, so an arm can be eligible while a flaky id differs. An id that never flakes in S but differs once in a parallel run makes the arm ineligible (conservative).

Not part of this trial (open plan items): the cause check of the job-time growth by step medians across merge dates; the targeted coupling-site controls (the audit alias at tests/test_extreme_gainer_audit.py:207 and the closed-port fixtures at tests/test_runtime_worker_openhands.py:1561); a module-provenance check of the coverage name collision (tests/test_broad_universe_coverage.py:30); and a background-steps arm. Only the S-versus-arm record comparison covers these sites.
Hosted wall-clock time on shared runners varies with queueing and neighbours. Three repeats with rotated order bound this but do not remove it. Job seconds are reported, not decisive.

The workflow, the locks, the controls, the oracle and the B1 fix are frozen here by hash. Any later edit to one of them must refreeze this record in the same commit: bumping TRIAL_BASE_SHA after a rebase, tightening a timeout or rewording the oracle all count. Run python3 scripts/validate_convergence.py --all-recorded --root . --json beside python3 scripts/validate.py before every push (docs/harness-defaults.md, anti-pattern row of 2026-10-02). If the head moves past base 56473e4b without a TRIAL_BASE_SHA bump, id_mapping fails and neither OS gets a verdict, so the draft pull request is not rebased.

Hosted logs carry runner home-directory paths in tracebacks. Logs retained as receipts must be sanitized first, because scripts/validate.py rejects home paths. Artifacts expire after 30 days and run records under the repository's 90-day retention, so the observed record keeps sanitized durable receipts in the repository rather than run links alone.
compare.py's docstring names CPython v3.13.16 by its annotated tag object (3b55c23f); this record pins the commit that tag dereferences to (cbc944f4).
The checker verifies declared consistency and artifact hashes, not truth or that this freeze preceded execution. The commit history and the hosted run timestamps show the order.

decision_and_scope.scope: Draft pull request PR-T only, never merged: the preregistered comparison of unittest-parallel 1.8.6 arms against the serial whole-suite command on GitHub-hosted macos-15 and ubuntu-24.04 runners at its head. Nothing is adopted under this planned record. validate-macos and validate keep their serial commands until an observed record meets the rule and PR-A (macOS) or PR-A2 (Linux) lands through the required checks.

rollback: Close the draft pull request. It is never merged, so main, the required checks, the rulesets and both production workflows stay unchanged; its artifacts expire after 30 days. If PR-A or PR-A2 is adopted later, reverting it restores the serial commands (python3 -m unittest -v on macOS, python3 -m unittest on Linux).
next_decision_changing_test: Push this branch once and open PR-T as a draft (lane:foundation, with the template's SOTA sources section filled in). It is never merged. Push again only to change a frozen input, because every push re-runs the whole trial: the paths filter compares the pull request's three-dot diff, which always contains the new workflow. When the compare job finishes, download result.json, checkout-status.json and summary.md, sanitize home paths out of any retained log, and write the observed record beside this one. It holds one native_cli_execution observation per timed arm-run: task whole-suite-macos-15 or whole-suite-ubuntu-24.04; role the arm (arm-s, arm-p3, and so on); condition baseline for S and candidate otherwise; attempt the repeat; command_index 0 to 6; one scope text per OS. A run's status is passed only when it exited 0 and is eligible under both oracle parts. Each observation keeps its hashed sanitized artifacts and the jobs API step and job seconds. Adopt within that OS's scope (PR-A for macos-15, PR-A2 for ubuntu-24.04) only if that OS's verdict is adopt under the rule above and id_mapping.ok is true. Otherwise record reject or no verdict as a failed attempt and keep the serial command.
